summary: The 2026-07-28 Authorization page defines transport-level (HTTP-only) OAuth 2.1 authorization; it is OPTIONAL, SHOULD be used on HTTP transports, SHOULD NOT on STDIO (index L19-25). Roles: MCP server = OAuth 2.1 resource server; MCP client = OAuth 2.1 client; authorization server (AS) is out of scope but must be discoverable (index L48-59). Servers MUST publish RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata (PRM) with >=1 authorization_servers and MUST expose it via WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata on 401 or a .well-known/oauth-protected-resource URI; clients MUST support both, must try RFC 8414 and OIDC discovery in a fixed order, and MUST validate issuer equality (index L74-82, disc L15-96). Client registration: CIMD SHOULD, pre-registration, DCR MAY (deprecated) (index L66-72, L94-97). Clients MUST use PKCE S256, MUST refuse if code_challenge_methods_supported is absent, MUST send RFC 8707 resource (canonical server URI) in authorization and token requests, MUST record the issuer and validate RFC 9207 iss per a four-row table before redeeming the code, MUST send Authorization: Bearer on every request and never in the query string. Servers MUST validate tokens per OAuth 2.1 §5.2, MUST enforce audience, MUST return 401 for invalid/expired tokens, 403 for insufficient scope (SHOULD carry WWW-Authenticate Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope, resource_metadata), 400 for malformed requests, MUST honor scope hierarchies, MUST NOT pass through tokens. Scope strategy: challenge scope is authoritative; fallback to PRM scopes_supported; step-up re-auth uses the union of previously requested and challenged scopes with retry limits. Refresh tokens: confidential storage, offline_access only via AS scopes_supported, never assumed. No JSON-RPC methods or MCP capabilities are defined by this page.

methods.name: HTTP: protected MCP request (bearer token)
methods.capability_gate: None. Authorization is transport-level; no MCP JSON-RPC capability (ClientCapabilities/ServerCapabilities) gates it (index L13-15, L19). Applies only to HTTP-based transports (index L21-23).
methods.params: HTTP request header `Authorization: Bearer <access-token>` (string, REQUIRED on every client->server HTTP request, index L264-271). Token MUST NOT appear in the URI query string (index L273). Only tokens issued by the MCP server's own AS may be sent (index L294). Body/method are the normal Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC payload (not defined on this page).
methods.result: HTTP 200 with normal MCP response if token valid (index L187-189); HTTP 401 if authorization required or token invalid/expired (index L291-292, L323); HTTP 403 for invalid scopes / insufficient permissions (index L324); HTTP 400 for malformed authorization request (index L325). No JSON-RPC-level resultType/CacheableResult/pagination aspects apply.
methods.notes: Client MUST be able to parse WWW-Authenticate and react to 401 (disc L51). Not a JSON-RPC method; listed because an SDK transport must implement it.

methods.name: HTTP: 401 Unauthorized challenge
methods.params: Response status 401. Header `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` with parameters: `resource_metadata="<PRM URI>"` (string URI; one of the two MUST-implement discovery mechanisms, disc L41-43, RFC 9728 §5.1); `scope="<space-separated scopes>"` (string, SHOULD be included, index L101-105; may be any relation to scopes_supported, index L107-109); RFC 6750 `error`/`error_description` are permitted by reference to RFC 6750 §3 (index L101-102) but the page enumerates only resource_metadata and scope for 401. Example: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", scope="files:read"` (index L120-124).
methods.result: Client extracts resource_metadata URL (index L154), fetches PRM, applies scope selection strategy (index L128-131).
methods.notes: If the server chooses the well-known-URI mechanism instead, a 401 without resource_metadata is allowed and the client MUST fall back to constructing well-known URIs (disc L45-49).

methods.name: HTTP: 403 insufficient_scope challenge
methods.params: Response status 403 (SHOULD, RFC 6750 §3.1) with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` parameters: `error="insufficient_scope"` (string constant), `scope="required_scope1 required_scope2"` (string, minimum scopes needed for the operation; SHOULD contain ALL scopes needed for the current operation in a single challenge; previously granted scopes need not be repeated), `resource_metadata="<PRM URI>"` (string, for consistency with 401), `error_description="..."` (string, optional, human-readable) (index L336-344, L346-361). Example index L373-379.
methods.result: Client SHOULD run the step-up flow: union(previously requested scopes, challenge scopes) -> re-authorize -> retry a bounded number of times (index L381-404).
methods.notes: Server MUST account for scope hierarchies when judging sufficiency (index L406-407). Server SHOULD NOT include `offline_access` in challenge scope (index L313-315).

methods.name: HTTP: GET Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728)
methods.capability_gate: None. Server MUST implement RFC 9728 (index L74, disc L15).
methods.params: GET to (a) the `resource_metadata` URI from WWW-Authenticate if present, else (b) `<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource<mcp-endpoint-path>` then (c) `<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, in that order (disc L43-49). No request parameters defined by MCP.
methods.result: JSON document per RFC 9728. Fields named by the MCP pages: `authorization_servers` (array of issuer URL strings, REQUIRED, >=1 entry, disc L16-17); `scopes_supported` (array of strings, OPTIONAL, used as fallback scope set and 'intended to represent the minimal set of scopes necessary for basic functionality', index L131-136; MUST NOT assume relation to challenge scopes, index L109); `resource` (the canonical resource identifier the client's RFC 8707 `resource` parameter aligns with, index L228-230). All other RFC 9728 fields are not enumerated by the MCP page.
methods.notes: Client selects the AS when several are listed (RFC 9728 §7.6, disc L23-27) and MUST keep separate registration state per AS (disc L32-35).

methods.name: HTTP: GET Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414 / OIDC Discovery)
methods.capability_gate: None. Client MUST support both RFC 8414 and OIDC Discovery (index L82); AS MUST offer at least one (index L77-80).
methods.params: For issuer with path (https://auth.example.com/tenant1) try in order: 1) https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/tenant1, 2) https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration/tenant1, 3) https://auth.example.com/tenant1/.well-known/openid-configuration. For issuer without path: 1) https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, 2) https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration (disc L77-95). Suffix is the default `oauth-authorization-server`; MCP defines no app-specific suffix (disc L59-63).
methods.result: JSON metadata. Fields named by the MCP pages: `issuer` (string, MUST be identical to the issuer identifier used to build the URL, else MUST NOT use the document, disc L96; recorded for RFC 9207 validation, index L194); `code_challenge_methods_supported` (array of strings; if ABSENT the client MUST refuse to proceed, for both RFC 8414 and OIDC documents, sec L56-60); `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported` (boolean, optional; true means the AS emits iss and the client MUST reject responses lacking iss, index L196, L200-205); `scopes_supported` (array of strings; `offline_access` MAY be requested only if listed here, index L310); `client_id_metadata_document_supported` (boolean, referenced by the client-registration page, not defined on the index page). Endpoint URL fields (authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, registration_endpoint) are RFC 8414 fields and are not enumerated on these pages.
methods.notes: Direction is client -> authorization server (a third party), listed as client->server for schema purposes.

methods.name: OAuth: Authorization request (browser redirect)
methods.capability_gate: None. Client MUST have obtained a client_id via CIMD, pre-registration or DCR first (index L94-97).
methods.params: Parameters named by the MCP pages: `resource` (string, REQUIRED, canonical MCP server URI, e.g. resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.example.com, index L219-254); `code_challenge` (PKCE, REQUIRED, index L178-179, sec L51) with method `S256` (sec L54; parameter name `code_challenge_method` comes from RFC 7636/OAuth 2.1, not spelled on the page); `scope` (string, per scope selection strategy; OMIT if no challenge scope and no scopes_supported, index L128-131; MAY add `offline_access`, index L310); `state` (SHOULD be used and verified, sec L76-77); `client_id` (HTTPS URL for CIMD, index L166-167); `redirect_uri` (MUST be registered; MUST be localhost or HTTPS, sec L44, L72). Standard OAuth parameters such as response_type=code are not enumerated on the MCP pages.
methods.result: Authorization response delivered to the redirect URI (see next entry).
methods.notes: Before redirecting, client MUST record the validated `issuer` in the same per-request record as the PKCE code_verifier and state (index L194).

methods.name: OAuth: Authorization response (redirect callback)
methods.params: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` query parameters (index L213): authorization `code` (index L182-183); `iss` (string, AS SHOULD include, also on error responses, index L196); `state` (echoed; client SHOULD discard mismatches, sec L76-77); error responses: `error`, `error_description`, `error_uri` (index L215).
methods.result: Client MUST apply the RFC 9207 §2.4 table before sending the code to any token endpoint: iss_supported=true & iss present -> simple string compare to recorded issuer; true & absent -> REJECT; false/absent & present -> compare; false/absent & absent -> proceed (index L198-205). No case folding, default-port elision, trailing-slash or percent-encoding normalization before comparison (index L213). On mismatch MUST NOT act on or display error/error_description/error_uri (index L215).
methods.notes: Future revision expected to upgrade AS iss inclusion to MUST (index L211).

methods.name: OAuth: Token request (authorization_code / refresh_token)
methods.params: Parameters named by the MCP pages: `code_verifier` (PKCE, index L185); `resource` (REQUIRED, same canonical URI as in the authorization request, index L222); `scope` (MAY include `offline_access` when in AS scopes_supported, index L310). Refresh: client SHOULD declare `refresh_token` in its `grant_types` client metadata (index L309). grant_type/code/redirect_uri/refresh_token parameter names are OAuth 2.1 standard and not enumerated on the page.
methods.result: Access token (+ optional refresh token) (index L186). Client MUST NOT assume a refresh token is issued (index L311). Token response field names (access_token, token_type, expires_in, refresh_token, scope) are not enumerated on the page.
methods.notes: Client MUST keep refresh tokens confidential in transit and storage (index L308). AS MUST rotate refresh tokens for public clients (sec L35).

requirements.text: Implementations using an HTTP-based transport conform to this authorization specification.
Implementations using STDIO transport follow this specification; they retrieve credentials from the environment instead.
Implementations using alternative transports follow established security best practices for their protocol.
Authorization servers implement OAuth 2.1 with appropriate security measures for confidential and public clients (AS is out of MCP scope; relevant if the SDK ships an AS helper).
Support OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00).
Support OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591); DCR is deprecated and retained only for AS that lack CIMD support.
Implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728).
Use OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata for authorization server discovery.
Support both AS metadata discovery mechanisms (RFC 8414 and OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0).
Follow the normative discovery requirements of the Authorization Server Discovery page.
Obtain a client ID via CIMD, pre-registration or DCR (per the Client Registration page's selection priority) before initiating the authorization flow.
Include a `scope` parameter in the WWW-Authenticate header (RFC 6750 §3) indicating the scopes required to access the resource.
Challenge scopes may equal, be a subset, superset, or an unrelated collection relative to `scopes_supported`.
Assume any particular set relationship between the challenged scope set and `scopes_supported`.
Treat the scopes provided in the WWW-Authenticate challenge as authoritative for the current operation.
When re-authorizing, include the challenge scopes alongside previously granted scopes to avoid losing permissions needed for other operations.
Strive for consistency in how scope sets are constructed; not required to surface every dynamically issued scope via `scopes_supported`.
Follow least privilege: request only scopes necessary for intended operations.

Initial scope selection priority: (1) `scope` from the initial 401 WWW-Authenticate header; (2) else all `scopes_supported` from PRM; omit the `scope` parameter entirely if `scopes_supported` is undefined.

Before redirecting the user-agent, record the `issuer` value from the selected AS's validated metadata and associate it with the same per-request record as the PKCE code verifier (and `state`, if used).
Authorization servers include the `iss` parameter in authorization responses, including error responses (RFC 9207 §2).
Authorization servers that include `iss` advertise `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true` in metadata.

Apply RFC 9207 §2.4 validation before transmitting the authorization code to any token endpoint: if metadata says supported=true and iss absent -> reject; if iss present (regardless of metadata) -> simple string comparison against recorded issuer; if supported false/absent and iss absent -> proceed.
Apply scheme/host case folding, default-port elision, trailing-slash or percent-encoding normalization to the decoded `iss` value before comparison.
On `iss` mismatch, act on or display `error`, `error_description`, or `error_uri` from an error authorization response.
Implement Resource Indicators (RFC 8707); the `resource` parameter MUST be in both authorization and token requests, MUST identify the target MCP server, and MUST use the server's canonical URI.
Provide the most specific URI possible for the MCP server as the `resource` value.
Accept uppercase scheme and host components in resource URIs for robustness, even though canonical form is lowercase.

Consistently use the canonical URI form without a trailing slash unless the slash is semantically significant. Canonical URI MUST have a scheme and MUST NOT contain a fragment (examples of invalid: `mcp.example.com`, `https://mcp.example.com#fragment`).
Send the `resource` parameter regardless of whether the AS supports it.
Use the `Authorization: Bearer <access-token>` request header (OAuth 2.1 §5.1.1) and include it in EVERY HTTP request from client to server.
Include access tokens in the URI query string.
Validate access tokens as described in OAuth 2.1 §5.2 before processing the request.

Validate that access tokens were issued specifically for this server as the intended audience (RFC 8707 §2); reject tokens that do not include the server in the audience claim or otherwise fail to prove the server is the intended recipient.
On token validation failure respond per OAuth 2.1 §5.3; invalid or expired tokens receive HTTP 401.
Send tokens to the MCP server other than ones issued by that MCP server's authorization server.
Only accept tokens valid for use with the server's own resources.
Accept or transit (pass through) any other tokens; when calling upstream APIs use a separate token issued by the upstream AS, never the token received from the MCP client.
Keep refresh tokens confidential in transit and storage (OAuth 2.1 §4.3).
Include `refresh_token` in the `grant_types` client metadata when refresh tokens are desired.
Add `offline_access` to the `scope` parameter of authorization and token requests only when the AS metadata lists it in `scopes_supported`.
Assume refresh tokens will be issued; the AS retains discretion.
Include `offline_access` in WWW-Authenticate `scope` or in PRM `scopes_supported`.
Return appropriate HTTP status codes for authorization errors: 401 (authorization required or token invalid), 403 (invalid scopes / insufficient permissions), 400 (malformed authorization request).
On insufficient scope at runtime respond 403 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="...", resource_metadata="..."` and optional `error_description`.
Include the scopes needed to satisfy the current operation in `scope`; previously granted scopes need not be included.
Include ALL scopes required for the current operation in a single challenge rather than challenging incrementally.
Be consistent in scope inclusion strategy and consider user-experience impact of scope choices.

Respond to scope-related errors (initial or runtime `insufficient_scope`) by requesting a new token with increased scopes via step-up authorization, or handle the error otherwise appropriately; clients acting on behalf of a user SHOULD attempt step-up.
Clients acting on their own behalf (`client_credentials`) attempt step-up or abort immediately.

Step-up flow: parse error info from AS response or WWW-Authenticate; determine required scopes as the UNION of previously requested scopes and the current challenge's scopes (scope accumulation is a client responsibility); re-authorize with that set; retry the original request no more than a few times, then treat as permanent authorization failure.
Also consult the Scope Selection Strategy for initial scope selection during step-up.
Implement retry limits and track scope-upgrade attempts per resource+operation combination to avoid repeated failures.
Account for scope hierarchies (a broader scope implies narrower ones) when deciding whether a token is sufficient.
Follow the normative Security Considerations page (audience binding, token theft, communication security, authorization code protection, mix-up, confused deputy, open redirection, CIMD security).
PRM document includes `authorization_servers` with at least one authorization server.
Maintain separate registration state (client credentials, tokens) per authorization server; MUST NOT assume credentials valid for one AS are accepted by another.
Implement at least one PRM discovery mechanism: `resource_metadata` in WWW-Authenticate on 401, or serve PRM at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[<endpoint path>]` or root.

Support both PRM discovery mechanisms: use the WWW-Authenticate `resource_metadata` URL when present, otherwise fall back to the path-suffixed well-known URI then the root well-known URI, in that order.
Be able to parse WWW-Authenticate headers and respond appropriately to HTTP 401 responses.
Attempt multiple AS metadata well-known endpoints in the specified priority order (path-insertion RFC 8414, path-insertion OIDC, path-appending OIDC; or RFC 8414 then OIDC for path-less issuers).
Validate AS metadata: `issuer` MUST be identical to the issuer identifier used to build the well-known URL; otherwise MUST NOT use the metadata.
Implement secure token storage and follow OAuth 2.1 §7.1 best practices.
All AS endpoints served over HTTPS; all redirect URIs either `localhost` or HTTPS (OAuth 2.1 §1.5).
Implement PKCE (OAuth 2.1 §7.5.2) and verify PKCE support before proceeding with authorization.
Use the `S256` code challenge method when technically capable.
Refuse to proceed if `code_challenge_methods_supported` is absent from AS metadata (both RFC 8414 and OIDC Discovery documents).
Have redirect URIs registered with the authorization server.
Use and verify `state` in the authorization code flow; discard results lacking or mismatching the original state.
MCP proxy servers using static client IDs obtain user consent for each dynamically registered client before forwarding to third-party AS.
Validate access tokens before processing and ensure no data is returned to unauthorized parties.

wire_details: Header (client->server, every request): `Authorization: Bearer <access-token>` (index L264-271). Never in query string (index L273).
Header (server->client) on 401: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<uri>", scope="<space-separated>"` (index L120-124; disc L43). Parameter names: `resource_metadata`, `scope`.

Header (server->client) on 403: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="<space-separated>", resource_metadata="<uri>", error_description="<text>"` (index L373-379). Constant: `error="insufficient_scope"`.

HTTP status codes: 401 Unauthorized (authorization required / token invalid or expired), 403 Forbidden (invalid scopes / insufficient permissions), 400 Bad Request (malformed authorization request) (index L319-325).
PRM JSON fields used: `authorization_servers` (required, >=1), `scopes_supported` (optional), `resource` (disc L16-17; index L131, L228-230).

AS metadata JSON fields used: `issuer` (must match), `code_challenge_methods_supported` (must be present), `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported` (boolean), `scopes_supported`; client-registration page adds `client_id_metadata_document_supported` (disc L96; sec L58-60; index L196, L310).

OAuth parameters: `resource` (RFC 8707; form-encoded, e.g. `&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.example.com`, index L248-252), `code_challenge`/`code_verifier` (PKCE), method constant `S256` (sec L54), `scope`, `state`, `iss` (RFC 9207), `offline_access` scope value (index L310), `refresh_token` grant type value in `grant_types` client metadata (index L309), `client_credentials` grant reference (index L385).
Authorization response encoding: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (index L213). `iss` comparison: simple string comparison RFC 3986 §6.2.1, no normalization (index L202-204, L213).
Canonical resource URI rules: absolute URI with scheme, lowercase scheme/host canonical (accept uppercase), no fragment, prefer no trailing slash; may include port and path (index L226-246).
Communication security: AS endpoints HTTPS only; redirect URIs `localhost` or HTTPS (sec L43-44).
No JSON-RPC error codes, `_meta` keys or MIME types are defined by the authorization page; authorization failures are pure HTTP-level.
sdk_implications: Client transport (Streamable HTTP): pluggable auth provider hook that injects `Authorization: Bearer` on every request (POST and any long-lived stream request), refuses to place tokens in query strings, and intercepts 401/403 responses before surfacing them as transport errors (index L264-273, L319-325).

Client: a WWW-Authenticate parser (RFC 6750 / RFC 9110 auth-param syntax, quoted strings, multiple challenges) extracting scheme `Bearer`, `resource_metadata`, `scope`, `error`, `error_description` (disc L51; index L336-344).

Client: PRM discovery with the exact fallback order (header URL -> path-suffixed well-known -> root well-known), JSON validation requiring non-empty `authorization_servers`, AS selection hook when several are listed, and per-issuer keyed storage of client credentials and tokens (disc L15-49).

Client: AS metadata discovery trying RFC 8414 and OIDC endpoints in the mandated order, with `issuer` equality check (reject on mismatch) and hard refusal when `code_challenge_methods_supported` is absent (disc L66-96; sec L56-60).

Client: PKCE generation (code_verifier, S256 challenge) and a per-authorization-request record holding code_verifier, state and the recorded issuer; RFC 9207 iss validation implementing the four-row table with strict string comparison before token exchange, and suppression of error/error_description/error_uri on mismatch (index L194-215; sec L51-54).

Client: RFC 8707 `resource` parameter builder producing the canonical server URI (scheme+host lowercase, optional port/path, no fragment, no trailing slash) and always sent in both authorization and token requests, even if the AS ignores it (index L219-254).

Client: scope strategy engine: initial scope = challenge scope else PRM scopes_supported else omit; step-up computes union(previously requested, challenged) and re-authorizes; bounded retries and per (resource, operation) attempt tracking; optional `offline_access` only when AS scopes_supported lists it (index L99-136, L381-404, L310).

Client: client registration abstraction with three strategies (CIMD hosted HTTPS URL client_id, static pre-registered credentials, deprecated DCR with `grant_types` including `refresh_token` and `application_type`), following the client-registration page's priority (index L66-72, L94-97, L309; changelog L44-50, L95-101).

Client: secure token store abstraction (refresh tokens confidential at rest; e.g. SecretManagement/DPAPI on Windows, keychain elsewhere) and a redirect-URI listener restricted to `localhost` or HTTPS with `state` verification (index L308; sec L31-32, L44, L72-77).

Server: bearer-token middleware for the HTTP transport that validates tokens per OAuth 2.1 §5.2 including audience binding to the server's canonical resource URI, returns 401 for missing/invalid/expired tokens with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=..., scope=...`, 403 with `error="insufficient_scope"` plus full required-scope list in one challenge, 400 for malformed requests, and never forwards the inbound token upstream (index L285-299, L319-379; sec L121-127).

Server: PRM endpoint helper serving `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/path]` JSON with `authorization_servers`, `resource`, optional `scopes_supported` (excluding `offline_access`), plus configuration of which discovery mechanism(s) to expose (disc L41-47; index L313-315).
Server: scope-check helper supporting scope hierarchies (broader implies narrower) and a stable, consistent challenge-scope computation per operation (index L354-366, L406-407).
Both: STDIO transport must NOT engage this flow; credentials come from the environment (index L22-23). Authorization must be opt-in/optional (index L19).

Conformance: the client suite `auth` (scenarios `auth/basic-dcr`, `auth/basic-metadata-var1`, extension `auth/client-credentials-jwt`, `auth/dpop`) drives the client via `MCP_CONFORMANCE_SCENARIO` and `MCP_CONFORMANCE_CONTEXT` env vars with the server URL as last CLI argument; the PowerShell client entrypoint must read these (conformance_README.md L318-326, L455-470; conformance_SDK_INTEGRATION.md L32-41, L79).
legacy_delta: NEW in 2026-07-28: RFC 9207 'Authorization Response Validation' section (record issuer, iss validation table, no-normalization rule, error suppression on mismatch); AS SHOULD emit `iss` and MUST advertise `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported` (index L192-215; changelog L40-43, SEP-2468). Absent in 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 (verified: 2025-11-25 page has no 'iss'/'9207' lines). RFC 9207 added to the Standards Compliance list.

NEW in 2026-07-28: Dynamic Client Registration is Deprecated (changelog L95-101, PR #2858); Overview item 3 now says 'MAY ... deprecated and retained for backwards compatibility'. 2025-11-25: CIMD SHOULD + DCR MAY (not deprecated). 2025-06-18: DCR SHOULD, no CIMD at all (2025-06-18 L60).

NEW in 2026-07-28: 'Refresh Tokens' section (confidential storage MUST, `refresh_token` in grant_types SHOULD, `offline_access` MAY only if in AS scopes_supported, MUST NOT assume issuance; servers SHOULD NOT advertise `offline_access`) (index L301-315). Not present in 2025-11-25 or 2025-06-18.

NEW in 2026-07-28: 'Servers MUST account for scope hierarchies' (index L406-407) and 'servers SHOULD include all scopes required for the current operation in a single challenge' (index L354-361). 2025-11-25 instead listed Minimum/Recommended/Extended server scope-inclusion approaches (2025-11-25 L523-527), now removed; 2025-11-25 said scope includes previously granted scopes to avoid loss, 2026-07-28 says servers 'are not required to include the client's previously granted scopes' and moves accumulation to the client (index L346-352, L368-369).

CHANGED in 2026-07-28: step-up flow step 2 now mandates union(previously requested scopes, challenge scopes); 2025-11-25 step 2 merely said 'Determine required scopes as outlined in Scope Selection Strategy' (2025-11-25 L554). Clients also now 'MUST treat challenge scopes as authoritative for the current operation' and 'SHOULD include these scopes alongside previously granted scopes when re-authorizing' (index L110-114); 2025-11-25 wording was 'authoritative for satisfying the current request' with no re-authorization clause.

CHANGED in 2026-07-28: Page split into sub-pages (authorization-server-discovery, client-registration, security-considerations); in 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 all of this was a single page. Security best practices moved from /specification/<rev>/basic/security_best_practices to /docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices.

CHANGED in 2026-07-28 (client-registration page, per changelog L44-50): clients MUST specify `application_type` in DCR (SEP-837) and MUST key persisted credentials by issuer, MUST NOT reuse across AS, MUST re-register when the AS changes (SEP-2352); discovery page now states per-AS separate registration state (disc L29-37). Not in 2025-11-25.

UNCHANGED across 2025-06-18 / 2025-11-25 / 2026-07-28: RFC 8707 `resource` MUST in both requests with canonical URI; Bearer header on every request, never in query; server MUST validate audience and return 401 on invalid/expired; MUST NOT pass through tokens; PKCE MUST; HTTPS/localhost redirect rules; 401/403/400 table.

2025-06-18 vs later: 2025-06-18 required WWW-Authenticate with resource_metadata on 401 as the ONLY PRM discovery mechanism (2025-06-18 L89) and only RFC 8414 AS metadata (L66-68, L96); 2025-11-25 added the well-known-URI alternative, OIDC discovery, the three-endpoint priority order, the Scope Selection Strategy, the 403 insufficient_scope / step-up sections, CIMD, and the explicit 'MUST verify PKCE support / code_challenge_methods_supported' rule (2025-06-18 L329 had PKCE MUST only). A dual-era client must therefore tolerate 2025-06-18 servers that never serve well-known PRM and 2025-06-18 AS that only publish RFC 8414 metadata, and 2025-11-25/2026-07-28 servers that omit resource_metadata from 401.

Wire-version interplay: authorization is independent of the JSON-RPC handshake change (stateless `_meta` in 2026-07-28 vs `initialize` in earlier revisions, changelog L14-18), but conformance runs auth scenarios once per revision on that revision's wire (conformance_README.md L132-145), so the auth layer must sit below the version-specific session layer.
